title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized lookups (.get(id=rule_id), .filter(project=project), .fetch_for_project(project)). No raw SQL or string interpolation is present.

The refactored convert_args method now scopes the rule lookup to the project derived from the URL (which is already validated by ProjectEndpoint and ProjectAlertRulePermission). For AlertRule it uses fetch_for_project(project) and for Rule it uses filter(project=project), then .get(id=rule_id). This prevents cross-project/cross-org IDOR: a rule_id belonging to another project will return DoesNotExist and raise NotFound. The new test 'test_cannot_mute_unowned_alert' confirms this behaviour. The previous code fetched by id alone (self.rule_model.objects.get(id=rule_id)) which was the IDOR vulnerability; the fix correctly closes it.
